text: God plans for us humans to work hard from the day of our birth until we are buried in the soil from which we were made.[92]
We don't understand life, so we worry and dread the day that it will end. *
And each of us is bothered by troubling feelings— from the king, seated on his glorious throne and wearing his crown and royal robes, *
to the homeless in the street, sitting in dirt and grime and wearing worn-out clothes.
We are angry, jealous, or hateful; or maybe we feel guilty or are afraid of death. Sometimes we are confused by a dream,
or lie awake worrying about our work, and so we get little rest.[93] We see ourselves running for our lives,
and almost reaching safety, then we wake up, amazed— it was all a dream.
The troubles that sinners have will be seven times worse than those of other people. Any living creature
can suffer a violent death when there is war or fighting, or they can die from disaster, horrible disease, or famine.
But God created these troubles to punish those who do wrong, as when he sent the flood.
Animals and humans were created from the soil, and will return to it, just as water returns to the sea.
What you gain by being honest will last forever, but wealth you get by bribery and cheating will disappear.
It will dry up like a stream in the summer heat, or quickly fade, like thunder from a passing storm.
And while generous people can celebrate success, those who disobey God will be failures.
Their children will be like trees growing out of a rocky cliff and having rotten roots and few branches.
They are like the tall grass that grows beside a stream— when the stream runs dry, the grass quickly withers.
But those who show kindness, especially to the poor, are gardens that always bloom with blessing after blessing.
It is good to have a job and earn your own money, but it is even better to discover hidden treasure.
Having wisdom is better than giving your name to your children or to a city that you have built. Cattle and fruit trees can bring you wealth,[94] but a happy marriage[95] is better than riches.
Wine and music bring happiness, but if you love wisdom, you will be even happier.
A pleasant voice is sweeter than the music of flutes and harps.
Our eyes like beauty and graceful movement, but most of all, we want to see our fields becoming green with sprouting wheat.
Having friends and neighbors is important, but being married is even better.
Relatives and friends can help when you are in trouble, but the best help comes from giving to the poor.
Gold and silver may give security, but they don't compare with good advice.
Many trust wealth and power, but if you obey the Lord, he will give you whatever you need if you will just ask.
If you obey the Lord, he will protect you and make your life a garden where blessings grow.
You would be better off dead than to be a beggar.
If you have to beg for food, your life isn't your own, and you won't have any respect for yourself. If you are smart and have learned anything, you won't beg.
No matter what beggars say, they really are ashamed of what they do.
